tasks.short: Gather orders, stock and equipment status before the meeting, confer with managers on requirements and schedules, enter the agreed work plan, and tell crew leads about changes.

steps.what: Farm supervisor gathers orders, stock and equipment status from e-mails and spreadsheets
Farm supervisor confers with managers to determine production requirements, equipment and supplies, and work schedules
Farm supervisor writes the agreed work plan: into the planning spreadsheet and daily lists by hand today; once into the planning screen after the change, with daily lists from the rules
Farm supervisor checks the daily harvest, pick and pack lists: quantities per order, dock times and crews match the agreed plan
Farm supervisor publishes the checked daily lists to the crew leads
Farm supervisor tells crew leads about schedule changes

tasks.design: Orders and stock arrive from the sales platform by API and equipment status from the maintenance list, and a planning screen ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the week's demand, stock and machines out of use, so the supervisor does not gather them from e-mails and spreadsheets before the meeting. Fixed rules turn the agreed plan and the orders into daily harvest, pick and pack lists per dock time, so the plan is entered once; the supervisor checks the lists and publishes them to the crew leads. Conferring with managers and telling crew leads stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders came by e-mail and the plan was kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Sales platforms deliver orders and stock by API; rules turn them into daily lists.
tasks.still_hard: Weather and late orders change the plan during the day.
tasks.human_edge: Telling managers what the crew can really manage this week.

reach.learn: Whether daily lists match the orders.

evidence.claim: Floriday lets growers manage stock and orders across sales channels and offers an API for software vendors.
Order-driven planning touches no AI Act Annex III area.

assumptions: Boundary: from the weekly meeting due to crew leads told; investment decisions are outside.
Input contract: orders arrive by API; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.

Meetings, checking and publishing the lists and telling crew leads keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 for reading the screen and orders that still come by e-mail. s3 keeps 70 because the supervisor still writes the agreed plan; only copying it into daily lists goes.
research_questions: Do late changes to the day's plan fall?

incremental.description: Farm supervisor keeps the planning rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The daily harvest, pick and pack lists exactly as checked by the supervisor in s3c, published once to the crew leads in the planning screen ({OPS_SYSTEM}); any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a farm with few, stable orders, many still by e-mail, and simple daily lists (7.3); high: a grower with many daily orders through the platform (16.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect time sheets, type hours into the hours spreadsheet, check the hours, send them to the payroll provider, judge evaluations, and fill personnel action forms.

steps.what: Workers check in and out with their badge at the entrance
Farm supervisor collects hours: paper time sheets from workers today; after the change chases only missing check-ins
Farm supervisor prepares time reports by typing hours into the hours spreadsheet
Farm supervisor checks the final hours against the roster and known absences and corrects errors
Farm supervisor releases the checked hours to the payroll provider: by e-mail today, by one release through the payroll link after the change
Farm supervisor judges workers' performance for evaluations, promotions and discipline
Farm supervisor maintains details of personnel actions on paper forms

tasks.design: Workers check in and out with a badge, and hours per row and batch are registered in the labour registration system ({HCM}), so paper time sheets are not collected or typed; the supervisor chases only missing check-ins. After checking, the supervisor releases the hours to the payroll provider through the system's payroll link ({PAYROLL}) instead of by e-mail. Hire, promotion, evaluation and discipline forms in the HR system fill name, contract and history from the person's record, so the supervisor writes only the judgement. Judging performance stays with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Hours were collected on paper, typed and mailed; personnel forms were filled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Badge registration feeds hours to payroll; HR forms fill from the person's record.
tasks.still_hard: Seasonal workers forget to check in.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding who is ready to lead a crew.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor checks hours and judges people instead of typing.

reach.learn: Whether hours arrive on time and correct.

evidence.claim: ProCC registers badge check-in and work per row, cart and batch, and sends hours live to Nmbrs or as XML to Loon.nl.
Badge registration that can check presence or pace needs works council consent.
Promotion or disciplinary decisions may not rest solely on automated processing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the week ended to actions recorded; pay calculation is outside.
Input contract: badge readers at the entrances; fallback is paper time sheets.

The supervisor checks hours before every payroll run; checking and judging keep their full time. s1 keeps 20 for chasing missing check-ins. s4 keeps 10 for the release. s6 keeps 70 because name, contract and history fill in, but the supervisor still writes each action and its reasons.
No pace norm is used to judge workers.

Badge registration of hours needs works council consent under WOR art 27; hours per row and batch are used for pay and costing, not to judge workers. Workers' badge time (s0, share 1) is outside the supervisor's savings.

incremental.description: Farm supervisor corrects missing or wrong check-ins.

approvals.approved_version: The week's hours per worker exactly as checked by the supervisor in s3, sent once through the payroll link to the payroll provider ({PAYROLL}) for that pay period; any correction needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many workers forget to badge or use entrances without readers, so the supervisor still collects and types about a third of the hours (34.4); high: badges cover nearly all hours (47.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check stock of supplies, decide what to buy, get prices from suppliers, fill the order, check it, send it, and receive the delivery.

steps.what: Farm supervisor scans the shelf label when supplies are issued from the shed
Farm supervisor checks stock of supplies: a full count in the shed today, spot checks against the system's list after the change
Farm supervisor decides which supplies such as insecticides, parts, lubricants or tools to buy
Farm supervisor phones suppliers for prices and delivery
Farm supervisor fills the purchase order
Farm supervisor checks the final purchase order: items, quantities and prices match what was decided, and the supplier and delivery address are right
Farm supervisor sends the checked order to the supplier: by e-mail today, by one release from the purchasing system after the change
Farm supervisor checks the delivery against the order and stores it

tasks.design: Supplies issued from the shed are booked out by scanning the shelf label in the purchasing system ({PROCUREMENT}), which keeps stock current and lists items below their minimum, so stock checks become spot checks. Regular suppliers' price lists with delivery times are loaded in the same system, so the supervisor phones only for items outside them, and the order is built from the chosen catalogue items. Once checked, the supervisor releases the order to the supplier from the system instead of by e-mail. Deciding what to buy and receiving deliveries stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was checked by eye, prices asked by phone and orders typed into e-mails.
tasks.enabler_now: Purchasing systems hold supplier price lists and send orders.
tasks.still_hard: Plant protection products change as authorisations change.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which pest will come early this year.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor decides purchases instead of chasing prices.

evidence.claim: Purchasing systems can hold supplier price lists with delivery times and send orders to suppliers.
Professional users of plant protection products need a licence and may use only authorised products.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock round to supplies stored; supplier contracts are outside.
Input contract: price lists kept current by the manager; fallback is phoning.

The supervisor checks every order. s1 keeps 50 for spot checks. s3 and s4 keep 40 for items outside the price lists. s6 keeps 20 for the release. Scanning issued supplies (s0, share 1) is the supervisor's added work.
Suppliers handle system orders as they did e-mails.

incremental.description: No further upkeep: scanning issued supplies is step s0, and the manager keeps the price lists.

approvals.approved_version: The purchase order with items, quantities and prices exactly as checked by the supervisor in s5, sent once from the purchasing system to the chosen supplier; any change needs a new check and release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many one-off parts from new suppliers, so prices are still phoned and orders typed (25.5); high: regular supplies from suppliers with loaded price lists (37.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect the contractor's work on site, meet the contractor, write the site visit report, track open issues, and report progress to the manager.

steps.what: Farm supervisor monitors construction of horticultural buildings or irrigation systems on site
Farm supervisor meets the contractor about progress and problems
Farm supervisor writes the site visit report with photos: as a document today, on a phone form with photos placed on the site plan after the change
Farm supervisor tracks open issues and chases the contractor: in a spreadsheet and by e-mail today, on the shared issue list after the change
Farm supervisor checks each new issue before it goes to the contractor: the problem, place, photo and deadline
Farm supervisor posts the checked issues to the list shared with the contractor
Contractor updates and closes their own issues on the shared list
Farm supervisor reports progress to the manager in the weekly meeting

tasks.design: Site visits are recorded on a phone form with photos placed on the site plan ({PROJECT}), instead of a written report. The supervisor checks each problem and posts it as an issue on a shared list with the contractor, who updates and closes their own issues, so the supervisor does not keep a spreadsheet and chase by e-mail. Inspecting, meeting the contractor and reporting to the manager stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were written after the visit and issues chased by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Site apps place photos on plans and share issue lists with contractors.
tasks.still_hard: Small contractors may not use the shared list.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that an irrigation pipe is laid with the wrong fall.

evidence.claim: Site apps can place photos on plans and share issue lists with contractors.

assumptions: Boundary: from the project underway to the manager informed; contract changes are outside.
Input contract: contractor has access to the issue list; fallback is e-mail.
Contractors update issues (s4k, share 1) in about the time replying to e-mails took; this is outside the supervisor's savings.

Site inspections, meetings, reporting and checking issues keep their full time. s3 keeps 80 because the supervisor still writes each finding; only arranging photos in a document goes. s4 keeps 50 because the spreadsheet and e-mail chasing go but the supervisor still follows open issues.

incremental.description: Farm supervisor sets up the issue list per project.

approvals.approved_version: The new issues with problem, place, photo and deadline exactly as checked by the supervisor in s4c, posted once to the issue list shared with the contractor ({PROJECT}); any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small repair project where the contractor keeps answering by e-mail (0.9); high: a large build where the contractor works the shared list (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The farm supervisor keeps conferring with managers, judging people, deciding purchases and inspecting projects; gathered status, typed hours, phoned prices and written reports shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor with more time on the farm floor.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
